intro: I speak about what agent systems can actually prove, not what they claim. Talks are technical, demo-led, and usually carry a negative result alongside the working one.

topics.title: Runtime governance for AI agents
topics.detail: Where enforcement sits between an agent's decision and its action, and what a policy gate can express that a prompt cannot.

topics.title: Hardware attestation, and its limits
topics.detail: Validated on live SEV-SNP, TDX and H100. Including the part most talks skip: no confidential computing silicon is proof against someone who owns the machine.

topics.title: Verifiable evidence and audit chains
topics.detail: Tamper-evident records a third party can check offline, and the difference between proving what happened and preventing it.

topics.title: Model weight custody
topics.detail: What changes when the model leaves your data center, and why open weights do not end the custody problem.

book.title: Architecting at Scale
book.line: Author of Architecting at Scale (Packt, 2026), a field guide to large-scale AI-native system design.
